catalog.name: Bio / NIH MCP server catalog
catalog.description: Curated, reviewed list of Model Context Protocol servers of interest to the biomedical and NIH/NIAID research community. Entries are third-party resources described by the curator, not publisher-attested ARD entries.

entries.description: One CLI binary and MCP server over a single command grammar reaching ~72 biomedical sources (PubMed/PubTator3/Europe PMC, ClinVar, MyVariant, gnomAD, ClinicalTrials.gov and NCI CTS, OpenFDA, ChEMBL, Open Targets, Reactome, UniProt, NIH RePORTER, CIViC, OncoKB and more), with cross-entity pivots and shipped skills.
representativeQueries: find recruiting clinical trials for BRAF V600E melanoma
what does ClinVar and gnomAD say about this variant
list recent PubMed articles linking a gene to a disease
which drugs target EGFR and what adverse events are reported for them
which NIH-funded projects study Lynch syndrome
entries.cat:auth: none for most sources; optional keys (e.g. S2_API_KEY, NCBI, OncoKB) unlock some features
entries.cat:install: uv tool install biomcp-cli && biomcp serve   # or: docker run --rm -i ghcr.io/genomoncology/biomcp serve
entries.cat:dataTerms: Upstream terms govern results; repo has a per-source licensing page (docs/reference/source-licensing.md). KEGG distinguishes academic vs non-academic use; COSMIC is indirect-only; OncoKB needs registration.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Strongest single entry. Very active (release 0.9.3 on PyPI 2026-10-18, 679 stars), clear data-terms documentation, Claude Code plugin + skills, BioASQ benchmark page. The MCP surface is small on purpose (7 tools in 0.9.3; earlier docs describe a single execution tool), which keeps context cost low. Install `biomcp-cli`, NOT the unrelated PyPI package `biomcp`. The README declares MCP Registry name io.github.genomoncology/biomcp but the official registry returned no such server on 2026-11-13. No public hosted endpoint; self-host for HTTP. Overlaps heavily with the cyanheads PubMed/ClinicalTrials servers below.

entries.description: MCP wrapper over the BioThings APIs (MyGene.info, MyVariant.info, MyChem.info, taxonomy) plus Entrez download helpers.
representativeQueries: get MyGene.info annotation for TP53
look up the variant rs7412 in MyVariant.info
find MyChem.info records for remdesivir
resolve the NCBI taxonomy entry for Plasmodium falciparum
entries.cat:dataTerms: BioThings APIs are free/open; underlying aggregated sources keep their own terms (e.g. some MyVariant sources are non-commercial).
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Works today (19 tools listed), MIT, 37 stars. But no commits for ~12 months, so treat as maintenance-mode. Fine-grained tools (19) cost more context than BioMCP, which already reaches MyGene/MyVariant/MyChem. Has local file-download tools that write to disk -- set an output dir. Part of the Holy Bio MCP bundle.

entries.description: NCBO BioPortal ontology search: find ontology terms/classes and properties across BioPortal's ontologies, plus ontology usage analytics.
representativeQueries: find the NCIT term for lung adenocarcinoma
which ontologies define a property called part_of
search Cell Ontology for T helper 17 cell
how often was the MONDO ontology viewed in BioPortal last year
entries.cat:auth: BioPortal API key (BIOPORTAL_API_KEY) for local use; hosted endpoint answered initialize/tools/list without a key
entries.cat:license: BSD-3-Clause (stated in README; GitHub shows no detected license file)
entries.cat:dataTerms: BioPortal terms of use apply; individual ontologies carry their own licenses (some restrict redistribution, e.g. SNOMED CT, MedDRA).
entries.cat:verifiedBy: remote Streamable HTTP handshake + tools/list (server bioportal_mcp)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Official NCBO repo (Stanford), small and focused (3 tools). Hosted on a fastmcp.app (FastMCP Cloud) URL rather than a bioontology.org domain, so availability depends on that deployment; no commits for ~11 months. Overlaps with EMBL-EBI OLS4 (default) -- keep this optional for NCIT/BioPortal-only ontologies.

entries.description: MCP wrapper for the gget bioinformatics library (Pachter lab), which gives one-line access to Ensembl search/info/sequence, BLAST/BLAT, MUSCLE/DIAMOND alignment, ARCHS4 expression, Enrichr, Bgee, PDB, AlphaFold, ELM, COSMIC, Open Targets and CELLxGENE.
representativeQueries: BLAST this protein sequence and show the top hits
get the Ensembl IDs and canonical transcript for ACE2
run Enrichr on this list of differentially expressed genes
which tissues express IFITM3 most highly according to ARCHS4
entries.cat:auth: none for most tools; COSMIC requires a COSMIC account
entries.cat:dataTerms: Per upstream; COSMIC is licensed (non-commercial academic free with registration); ELM is academic-use.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: local stdio handshake + tools/list (20 tools incl. gget_setup)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: About gget: a widely used Python/CLI toolkit (Luebbert & Pachter, Bioinformatics 2023) that wraps many genomic web services behind short commands -- this MCP exposes those commands as tools. Works today; MIT; 33 stars. Wrapper last released 2025-10 while gget itself is at 0.30.8 (2026-06), so the wrapper may lag gget. Some tools (BLAST, AlphaFold, gget_setup) are slow or install heavy dependencies; gget_cosmic needs credentials. Good optional sequence/alignment toolbox.

entries.description: Read-only SQL access to the OpenGenes database of aging/longevity-associated genes (lifespan experiments, gene-hallmark links, longevity associations).
representativeQueries: which genes extend lifespan in mice when overexpressed
list longevity-associated variants reported for FOXO3
what aging hallmarks are linked to SIRT6
entries.cat:auth: none (downloads data snapshot from Hugging Face longevity-genie/bio-mcp-data)
entries.cat:dataTerms: OpenGenes data terms apply; snapshot is redistributed by the wrapper authors -- check currency against open-genes.com.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Niche (aging biology), not core NIH/NIAID. Works, MIT, 21 stars, but ~13 months without commits and serves a frozen SQLite snapshot rather than the live database. Text-to-SQL pattern is clean (schema + example-query tools). Optional.

entries.description: Read-only SQL access to SynergyAge, a curated database of synergistic, antagonistic and additive genetic interventions affecting lifespan in model organisms.
representativeQueries: which double mutants in C. elegans show synergistic lifespan extension
list epistatic interactions involving daf-2
entries.cat:auth: none (downloads data snapshot from Hugging Face)
entries.cat:dataTerms: SynergyAge terms apply; frozen snapshot.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Runs, but: only PyPI release is 0.1.0 (2025-06), last commit 2025-08, 10 stars, and the README is out of sync with the published package (`synergy-age-mcp stdio` exits with "unrecognized arguments"; plain `uvx synergy-age-mcp` works). README also has malformed `httpss://` links. Very narrow scope. Watch only.

entries.description: General-purpose biomedical AI agent (A1) with a large tool library, a data lake and a know-how library. It is an agent, not a hosted MCP server: it can import external MCP servers, and can export chosen Biomni tool modules as a local stdio MCP server via agent.create_mcp_server(tool_modules=[...]).
representativeQueries: prioritize candidate genes for a CRISPR screen on T cell exhaustion
query biomedical databases for genes linked to a GWAS trait
cat:transport: stdio (only when you write a small Python launcher)
entries.cat:auth: needs an LLM provider key for the agent itself; module export does not
entries.cat:install: conda env (biomni_e1) + pip install biomni; then a Python script calling A1().create_mcp_server(...).run(transport='stdio')
entries.cat:license: Apache-2.0 (code); README warns some integrated tools/databases carry more restrictive commercial licenses
entries.cat:dataTerms: Mixed; README says review each component before commercial use. Know-How library tracks commercial-use flags.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: repo + docs/mcp_integration.md read; not run (heavy env)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Impressive and very active (4,079 stars), but recorded accurately: biomni.stanford.edu is a web UI for the agent, and there is no published MCP endpoint, package entry point, or registry listing. To use it as an MCP server you build the environment (large), download an ~11 GB data lake, and export modules yourself. More useful as an MCP *consumer* that could load this catalog's servers. Watch.

entries.description: Public read-only MCP for the NIAID-funded BRC Analytics platform: organisms, assemblies, Galaxy workflow catalog and compatibility, ENA and SRA search, and Logan k-mer search jobs.
representativeQueries: which genome assemblies are available for Mycobacterium tuberculosis
what Galaxy workflows can run variant calling on this assembly
find SRA runs for dengue virus from Brazil
search ENA for sequencing studies on Candida auris
entries.cat:install: remote: add https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/ as a Streamable HTTP server
entries.cat:dataTerms: Public INSDC data (ENA/SRA) -- open; cite BRC Analytics and original submitters.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: remote handshake + tools/list (server BRC Analytics 3.4.10, 21 tools)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: The most NIAID-relevant server here: institutional, hosted, no auth, actively developed (Galaxy project). Read-only except logan_submit, which starts a remote search job. Does not launch Galaxy workflows itself -- pair with Galaxy MCP for that.

entries.description: MCP server for the NIAID Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center: Solr data queries, analysis job submission (assembly, annotation, BLAST, etc.) and workspace tools.
representativeQueries: find all Klebsiella pneumoniae genomes with carbapenem resistance genes in BV-BRC
submit a genome annotation job for this assembly
list the files in my BV-BRC workspace
entries.cat:dataTerms: BV-BRC terms of use; private workspace data requires your account.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: probe failed: dev-7 host returned Cloudflare 403 (python client) / 404 (curl) to unauthenticated initialize
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Highly relevant to NIAID but not ready: documented endpoint is a dev host, unauthenticated handshake did not succeed on 2026-11-13, repo has 0 stars, no license file, and no commits since 2026-02. Re-check; ask BV-BRC for a production URL.

entries.description: Life-science MCP over the RDF Portal: SPARQL across 50+ databases, entity search for UniProt, PubChem, PDB, MeSH, Reactome, Rhea, ChEMBL, TogoVar, NCBI E-utilities, and TogoID identifier conversion across 65+ ID systems.
representativeQueries: convert these UniProt accessions to NCBI Gene IDs
write and run a SPARQL query for human proteins annotated with a GO term
search PubChem and ChEMBL for compounds similar to oseltamivir
find NCBI records for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein structures
entries.cat:dataTerms: Per database; KEGG tools are disabled on the hosted server (academic-only license, local stdio opt-in).
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Excellent FAIR fit: SPARQL + identifier mapping + a query-provenance workflow; published (Kinjo et al., Database 2026). All tools annotated read-only. 33 tools is on the heavy side; its usage-guide tool helps the agent choose.

entries.description: EMBL-EBI hosted MCP for OLS4: search the biomedical ontologies indexed by OLS, walk ancestors/descendants, and embedding-based similar-class search.
representativeQueries: find the MONDO term for tuberculosis and its parent classes
list descendants of 'viral infectious disease' in the Disease Ontology
which ontology terms are semantically similar to 'cytokine storm'
entries.cat:license: OLS is Apache-2.0 open source; hosted service under EMBL-EBI terms of use
cat:dataSources: OLS4 ontology index (OBO Foundry and others)
entries.cat:dataTerms: EMBL-EBI terms of use; each ontology keeps its own license.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Institutional, hosted, no auth. Note the endpoint is /ols4/api/mcp; /ols4/mcp is the human docs page (POST returns 405). Ontology grounding is the cheapest way to reduce hallucinated terms, hence default. Also listed by Cracking Shells' interim list.
entries.cat:foundVia: prior report (sec. 3.3); confirmed by CrackingShells/mcp-servers list

entries.description: EMBL-EBI hosted MCP for InterPro: protein families, domains, domain architectures, GO-term search, taxonomic distribution and sequence analysis.
representativeQueries: what domains does this protein sequence contain
which proteins share the domain architecture of human ACE2
show the taxonomic distribution of the Pfam family PF00069
entries.cat:license: hosted service under EMBL-EBI terms of use
entries.cat:dataTerms: InterPro data is CC0; member databases keep their own terms.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Institutional and hosted; version 0.1.0 suggests early. No public source repo identified.

entries.description: Official Protein Data Bank in Europe MCP servers: PDBe API, search, apps and the PDBe graph database (Cypher) for structures, ligands, interactions and annotations.
representativeQueries: find X-ray structures for UniProt P0DTC2 below 2.5 angstrom resolution
which ligands bind the SARS-CoV-2 main protease in PDB entries
write a graph query for structures sharing a binding site with this ligand
entries.cat:install: uvx pdbe-mcp-server --server-type pdbe_api_server   # or remote beta URL
entries.cat:dataTerms: PDB data are CC0.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: remote handshake + tools/list on beta host (60 tools for server-type all)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Official, active (44 stars). The hosted URL is a *wwwdev* beta whose interface may change, and the `all` server exposes 60 auto-generated tools -- prefer a narrower --server-type locally to limit tool overload.

entries.description: Official Open Targets MCP: entity search plus schema-guided GraphQL queries over target-disease associations, genetics, drugs and safety evidence.
representativeQueries: what are the top targets associated with systemic lupus erythematosus
what genetic evidence links IL23R to Crohn's disease
which approved drugs target JAK1 and for what indications
entries.cat:dataTerms: Open Targets Platform data are CC0.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Official (Open Targets with Anthropic, announced 2026-01-12); small tool surface; labelled experimental. Repo was renamed (open-targets-platform-mcp -> platform-mcp).

entries.description: Official Galaxy project MCP: connect to any Galaxy instance, manage histories and datasets, search and run Galaxy tools and workflows.
representativeQueries: upload these FASTQ files to a new Galaxy history and run FastQC
find a Galaxy tool for viral genome assembly and show its inputs
check the status and logs of my last Galaxy job
entries.cat:auth: Galaxy API key (GALAXY_URL + GALAXY_API_KEY) or OAuth in HTTP mode
entries.cat:dataTerms: Galaxy server terms; your histories are your data.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: repo/PyPI/registry checked; not run (needs a Galaxy API key)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: The execution half that BRC Analytics lacks. Write-capable (creates histories, runs jobs) -- keep optional and scope the API key. Has an experimental 3-tool discovery mode. The official registry entry is stale (1.3.0 vs PyPI 1.12.0).

entries.description: Mega-server of 2,700+ scientific tools (databases, ML models, literature search) for AI-scientist systems, with a compact mode that exposes only a few discovery tools.
representativeQueries: find a tool that predicts drug-target binding and run it on this compound
search Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar for recent papers on H5N1 transmission
what does FDA labeling say about drug interactions for nirmatrelvir
entries.cat:auth: none for most tools; some tools need provider keys
entries.cat:dataTerms: Per tool/upstream.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Very active (1,789 stars), paper on arXiv (2509.23426). Breadth is the risk: use compact mode or category filters or it floods context. Capabilities left blank on purpose (too many to list; depends on mode).

entries.description: Search PubMed and Europe PMC, fetch metadata and full text (PMC/EPMC/Unpaywall), citations and citation metrics, MeSH lookup and ID conversion.
representativeQueries: find 2026 PubMed reviews on long COVID immunology
fetch the full text of PMC article PMC1234567 and summarize the methods
format these PMIDs as APA citations
what MeSH terms describe antimicrobial resistance
entries.cat:auth: none (optional NCBI API key when self-hosted)
entries.cat:dataTerms: NCBI E-utilities usage policy (rate limits, tool/email); article text copyright per publisher.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Well-engineered, very active (168 stars), listed in the official registry. Hosted endpoint is an individual developer's domain -- fine for exploration, self-host for anything you depend on. Overlaps BioMCP's literature leg.

entries.description: Search ClinicalTrials.gov (API v2), fetch study records and posted results, field definitions and counts, and match patient profiles to candidate trials.
representativeQueries: how many NIAID-sponsored HIV vaccine trials are recruiting
get posted results for NCT04368728
find trials an adult with treatment-resistant tuberculosis might qualify for
entries.cat:dataTerms: ClinicalTrials.gov data are public (NLM terms and disclaimer apply).
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Deeper trials surface than BioMCP (results, eligibility matching). Same single-maintainer hosting caveat as the PubMed server.

entries.description: Search UniProtKB, fetch entries and sequences, map IDs, and look up proteomes and taxonomy.
representativeQueries: get the reviewed UniProt entry for influenza A hemagglutinin H5
map these UniProt accessions to Ensembl gene IDs
fetch the reference proteome for Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv
entries.cat:dataTerms: UniProt data are CC BY 4.0.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Young (0.4.0, 2 stars) but same well-tested framework as the PubMed server. TogoMCP also covers UniProt search; keep optional.

entries.description: Look up genes, fetch sequences, predict variant consequences (VEP), find orthologs and cross-references from Ensembl REST.
representativeQueries: predict the consequence of this variant with VEP
find mouse orthologs of human IFNAR1
get the genomic sequence of chr17:43044295-43125483 in GRCh38
entries.cat:dataTerms: Ensembl data are freely available without restriction.
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Young (3 stars). Overlaps gget-mcp's Ensembl tools but is more current and hosted.

entries.description: Unofficial MCP pack for NIH RePORTER: search projects and publications, award histories, new awards, funding concentration and expirations, SBIR portfolios.
representativeQueries: which NIAID R01 grants on antimicrobial resistance started in 2026
list publications linked to this NIH project number
which NIH grants on tuberculosis expire next year
entries.cat:dataTerms: RePORTER data are public.
entries.cat:verifiedBy: remote handshake + tools/list (53 tools, only 9 NIH-specific)
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Only dedicated RePORTER MCP verified, but the endpoint also injects ~44 unrelated gateway tools (prediction-market analytics, memory remember/recall, web research) and the repo is maintained by an automated agent fleet. Not institutional. BioMCP already reaches NIH RePORTER for gene/disease pivots. Watch; prefer a cleaner RePORTER server if one appears.

entries.description: ARD manifest for the niaid-blueprint agent plugin and its 12 Agent Skills (FAIR assessment, dataset metadata intake and extraction, citation, SHACL validation and rules, API/sitemap/robots.txt/llms.txt checks, teaching, and model-influence disclosure) for implementing the NIAID Blueprint for Digital Objects.
representativeQueries: find agent skills for the NIAID Blueprint
assess my repository against the NIAID Blueprint
which skills generate schema.org Dataset JSON-LD for NIAID
entries.cat:verifiedBy: niaid-blueprint/ard.json generated by yaml2ard.py; 0 errors and ARD conformance CLI PASS
entries.cat:reviewNotes: Same repository and maintainer as this catalog. Built from niaid-blueprint/catalog.yaml. The raw URL resolves once niaid-blueprint/ard.json is on master.
